articles.title: UFC 331: Tsarukyan se la juega y el peso mosca busca un cambio generacional
articles.standfirst: Esta noche se celebrará en Los Ángeles una de las carteleras más esperadas del año
articles.summary: Esta noche se celebrará en Los Ángeles una de las carteleras más esperadas del año
articles.body: Llegó el día. Esta noche Los Ángeles se vestirá de gala para celebrar el UFC 331, una cartelera numerada llena de nombres propios y de combates que darán mucho que hablar. La pelea estelar tendra un título en juego, el de peso mosca, y se lo disputarán Joshua Van (17-2) y Alexandre Pantoja (30-6) en una revancha muy esperada. Además, Arman Tsarukyan (23-3) vuelve al octágono casi un año después en el combate co estelar para medirse a Mauricio Ruffy (14-2) y acercarse al título de peso ligero. El duelo entre Pantoja y Van tiene todos los alicientes que necesita una pelea estelar para llamar la atención. En el primer combate, el brasileño se dislocó el codo en el primer asalto y perdió el título contra todo pronóstico. Por tanto, esta vez se verá de una vez por todas si lo del birmano fue un golpe de suerte o está preparado para dar un cambio generacional. Ambos han llevado su beef al siguiente nivel, son entretenidos de ver y tienen estilos totalmente diferentes, por lo que el espectáculo está asegurado. 24 años contra 36, la experiencia contra el hambre de ganar, el legado construido contra el legado por construir. El combate entre Tsarukyan y Ruffy tampoco se queda atrás, ya que podría definir al siguiente retador de peso ligero. Arman está obligado a ganar si no quiere dar aún más motivos a la UFC para olvidarse de él, ante un peleador que ha aceptado el combate en corto aviso y que no tiene nada que perder. Para el peleador armenio será un todo o nada, mientras que Ruffy sabe que el mero hecho de haber aceptado el reto ya le traerá beneficios en un futuro. De nuevo, otro choque de estilos. El striking estilístico de Mauricio contra el grappling de élite de Arman. Sin embargo, la cartelera no se queda aquí, ya que hay otros nombres que es importante remarcar para entender la magnitud del evento. Uno de ellos es el de Gable Stevenson (4-0), medallista de oro olímpico en lucha en Tokio 2021 y pupilo de Jon Jones, que se medirá a Sean Sharaf (4-2) con la intención de mantener su 100% de finalizaciones en el primer asalto y de paso acercarse de lleno al top 15 de la división. Tiene todos los ingredientes para ser una superestrella. Otro peleador destinado a llegar lejos en su carrera es Iwo Barianiewski (9-0), que tendrá en Alonzo Menifield (18-6-1) su primer gran reto para meterse de lleno en el top 15 de peso semipesado. Hasta el momento, el polaco suma tres combates en la UFC y tres K.O. en menos de minuto y medio. Hablando de K.O., el UFC 331 también supondrá el regreso a la compañía de Robelis Despaigne (6-2), medallista olímpico en Taekwondo, que se medira a Tai Tuivasa (15-10) en un duelo de acción asegurada. 'Bam Bam' está a una derrota de igualar a Tony Ferguson con la peor racha de la historia de la UFC, mientras que el cubano quiere demostrar su mejora en las MMA para asentarse en el peso pesado. En líneas generales, este evento lo tiene todo para hacer las delicias del respetable. Peleas mediáticas, enfrentamientos por el cinturón, y muchos nombres con un futuro prometedor que suponen una mezcla ideal para que esta madrugada todo el mundo esté atento. Además, una victoria de Tsarukyan podría acercarle a un futuro duelo contra Ilia Topuria, por lo que podría tener un impacto directo en el peleador hispanogeorgiano.

articles.title: Ayoub Ghadfa: "Lo que les molesta es que soy moro y estoy representando a España"
articles.standfirst: El boxeador, nacido en Marbella y que fue plata olímpica en París 2024, usa sus redes sociales para denunciar racismo tras dar su opinión sobre la situación en Ceuta en un podcast
articles.summary: El boxeador, nacido en Marbella y que fue plata olímpica en París 2024, usa sus redes sociales para denunciar racismo tras dar su opinión sobre la situación en Ceuta en un podcast
articles.body: Ayoub Ghadfa nació en Marbella. Sus padres, de origen marroquí, se habían trasladado a vivir a España en busca de un futuro mejor. Su progenitor es de Casablanca y su madre, de Fez. Por eso Ayoub se siente español y marroquí. El marbellí compite desde hace años por el país en el que nació y al que ha dado grandes alegrías. Campeón de Europa del superpesado (+92 Kg) en 2024, bronce mundial en 2023 y plata europea en 2022. Pero su mayor éxito para España, sin duda, ha sido la plata olímpica en París 2024. Pese a su exitoso currículum defendiendo los colores de España al máximo nivel, el boxeador malagueño ha denunciado comentarios racistas en sus redes sociales tras unas declaraciones sobre la crisis migratoria en Ceuta con Adel en un podcast. En él, Ghadfa dijo que opinaba "como marroquí, no como español". "Estoy avergonzado, nos avergüenzan de tal forma que eso parecía una jungla. No podía verlo. Yo estaba con mi padre, puse las noticias un día y dije ya. Porque ahora todos los moros somos invasores, somos delincuentes, todos somos unos violadores porque cuatro subnormales se dedican a hacer lo que hacen. No es justo que la gente piense así", dijo. Sus palabras obtuvieron por respuesta comentarios racistas. Él mostró algunos en su vídeo de Instagram en el que se pueden leer: "La nacionalidad te la da la sangre, nunca serás español", "Español de segunda", "Es marroquí, no regalemos la nacionalidad", "Eres moro, no español aunque hayas nacido aquí por desgracia". "Que le deporten"... Ghadfa ha reconocido en sus redes sociales que, aunque no suele responder a este tipo de comentarios, los hace porque está "bastante cansado" (...). "Y no pongo más comentarios porque creo que no merece la pena dedicarles tiempo", añade. En un post que titula 'A palabras necias, oídos sordos", el boxeador se dirige en un vídeo directamente a quienes opinan así. "No entiendo por qué la gente me critica o me juzga. ¿Qué criterio tiene para juzgarme o para decir si soy o no soy español? Realmente ellos, ¿qué han hecho por España? Probablemente no hayan hecho nada. Simplemente decir que son españoles. Sólo decir yo soy español y ya. Porque lo que realmente les jode, lo que realmente les molesta es que yo, que soy moro, estoy representando a España, me está yendo bien y les está representando a ellos también", dice. Y continúa: "La gente como vosotros, la gente así, no tiene ninguna aspiración en la vida. La gente como vosotros lo único que hace es sembrar el odio y yo creo que eso no es nada bueno, ya sea en España, ya sea en cualquier otro país. Y decirme que soy marroquí o que soy un moro, realmente a mí eso no me ofende, al revés, me enorgullece. Al igual que me siento orgulloso de ser español, porque España es mi casa y no necesito otro permiso para quererla ni para representarla. Así que como me enseñaron en el instituto, a palabras necias, oídos sordos", zanja.

articles.title: Isaac Okoh: Commonwealth Games gold medallist begins European Championship campaign | 'I can beat anyone in the world'
articles.summary: The European Boxing Championships are under way in Sofia, Bulgaria; Great Britain has a strong team in the competition with heavyweight Isaac Okoh looking to continue his winning run when he has his first bout in the event on Sunday; Okoh is the Commonwealth Games gold medallist
articles.body:
After underwhelming at the World Championships a year ago, Okoh has been on a fantastic winning run which culminated in a Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow.

He now wants to keep the momentum rolling into the European Championships, which are under way in Sofia.

Okoh has his first bout in Bulgaria on Sunday against Poland's Alexey Sevostyanov.

"I'm confident I can beat anyone in the world at the minute. It's going to take a really good fighter to beat me," Okoh told Sky Sports .

"There's a lot of great competitors at the weight. I feel like I'm up there and I'm in real contention for a gold medal.

"I'm well up for it and I fancy my chances against anyone at this tournament."

His victory in Glasgow has buoyed that confidence. "It's a dream come true, When you first start boxing the Commonwealth Games is one of the tournaments you dream of going to and then obviously to bring home the gold medal not too far away from home with friends and family there, it's a proud moment," Okoh said.

"It fills you with confidence going on into the future, Olympic qualifiers round the corner and the Olympics two years away.

"Since the World championships I've been boxing brilliantly. I knew I had to… I've been flying."

Britain has a strong team at these European championships.

"We've got a great squad. We had a brilliant medal tally coming back from the Commonwealths, one of the best in a long time. We've got a great squad at the minute, lots of talent, very young, fresh, hungry. So the mood's brilliant in camp and morale's through the roof," Okoh said.

"It's a great team and a great group of people to be around."

Although Sacha Hickey suffered a surprise loss to Croatia's Sara Beram, fellow Commonwealth Games medallist Ruby White got off to a strong start.

After losing in the flyweight final in Glasgow, White returned to action on Saturday and dominated Serbia's Nikolina Dzida, handing her counts in the first and second rounds en route to taking a clear unanimous decision.

articles.title: Caio Borralho: Arman Tsarukyan ‘going to get knocked out’ if he tries to strike with Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331
articles.summary: Mauricio Ruffy has scored back-to-back knockouts going into UFC 331
articles.body:
Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy co-headline UFC 331 in a match that could determine the next in line for a shot at the lightweight title in 2027, and Ruffy's former teammate Caio Borralho sees the Brazilian with the edge on the feet.

Tsarukyan spent the last few months competing in wrestling and grappling matches outside the UFC while waiting for a date and opponent to re-enter the octagon, and Ruffy was selected as his next foe in Los Angeles on Saturday. Tsarukyan has won his past five in the UFC, capped off by victories over Charles Oliveira and Dan Hooker, while Ruffy floored Rafael Fiziev and Michael Chandler with violent knockouts in 2026.

"I think both guys are dangerous for themselves," Borralho told MMA Fighting. "I think Ruffy has the one-shot knockout power that he can turn off anyone in the division. I think if Arman wants to strike him, even if it's a little bit, he's going to get knocked out. But I think if he's trying he's trying to wrestle at least the first two or three rounds, I think it's going to be harder for Mauricio to keep the pace and strategy, the calm."

Borralho thinks it's "a 50-50 fight," breaking it down similar how his teammate Carlos Prates' potential welterweight title bout with Islam Makhachev might go.

"I think it's a dangerous matchup for both guys," Borralho said of Prates vs. Makhachev. "I don't think Makhachev ever fought a guy like Prates that hurts you, makes you feel pain and other stuff with the leg kicks and all the stuff. On the other way, [Makhachev] has the grappling. This is the antidote to the striking, right? I think it's a hard matchup for both guys.

"If Prates manages to keep his composure when he gets taken down, like he always keeps, his mentality is very good when he's on the bottom, and get up and defend a couple takedowns or at least make Makhachev a little bit more tired—I think Makhachev is actually getting used to the new weight class, so I think he's carrying more mass, more muscle, so this takes some time for him to adjust to that."

Makhachev recently defended his 170-pound title with a decision over Ian Machado Garry, improving to 2-0 at welterweight since vacating the UFC lightweight throne. Prates, who has only lost once in the UFC against Garry, scored knockouts in every other fight in the UFC and Contender Series.

"We saw [Makhachev] got tired in his last fight like he's not used to," Borralho said, "And I think if got tired like that against a guy like Carlos, he's gonna get hurt. But I think he has a massive chance to finish this fight too, to submit Carlos or anything like that, because he has a very good jiu-jitsu. But, in general, hard matchup for both guys."

articles.title: UFC 331 'Embedded,' No. 6: Volkanovski forecasts Tsarukyan upset loss
articles.summary: The sixth and final episode of UFC 331 "Embedded" sees the headliners cut weight, face off and give final words before fight night.
articles.body:
The UFC is back on the Best Coast for UFC 331 , its eighth numbered event of the calendar year, and a flyweight title rematch headlines the card.

The popular "Embedded" fight week video series is here to document what's happening behind the scenes. UFC 331 ( Paramount+ ) takes place Saturday at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

In the main event, flyweight champion Joshua Van (17-2 MMA, 10-1 UFC) puts his title on the line the man he beat to win it, Alexandre Pantoja (30-6 MMA, 14-4 UFC), who is returning for the first time since the injury he suffered in the loss to Van. In the co-feature, the Mauricio Ruffy (14-2 MMA, 5-1 UFC) vs. Arman Tsarukyan (23-3 MMA, 10-2 UFC) winner could be next in line for the lightweight title.

The sixth and final episode of "Embedded" follows the featured fighters while they get ready for fight week. Here is the UFC's description of the episode from YouTube:

Alexandre Pantoja cuts weight with his family by his side; Giga Chikadze sheds the final pounds at the athlete hotel; UFC 331 athletes step on the scale for official weigh-ins; Mauricio Ruffy refuels and catches up with featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski ; Arman Tsarukyan enjoys a meal prepared by a Michelin-starred chef; the fighters face off one last time at the ceremonial weigh-ins at Crypto.com Arena.

articles.title: UFC 331 Live Updates, Highlights and Results
articles.summary: Joshua Van and Alexandre Pantoja are finally going to settle their score.
articles.body:
Joshua Van and Alexandre Pantoja are finally going to settle their score.

The two flyweights first met in late 2025, in a fight that saw Van take the division's title after Pantoja suffered a fluke arm injury less than 30 seconds into the first round. Tonight, in the main event of UFC 331 in Los Angeles, they will finally run it back, with flyweight gold once again on the line.

The UFC 331 co-main event is also a huge fight, as Arman Tsarukyan takes on Mauricio Ruffy at lightweight. Both men are among the top contenders in the division, and could conceivably set themselves up for a title shot in victory. That's particularly true in the case of Tsarukyan, who arguably should have already had that opportunity.

Tonight's card features plenty of other exciting matchups. The main card will be highlighted by a fan-friendly bantamweight clash between Patricio "Pitbull" Freire and "The Korean Superboy" Doo Ho Choi. It will also include the latest appearances from unbeaten prospects Iwo Baraniewski and Gable Steveson, who will take on on Alonzo Menifield at light heavyweight and Sean Sharaf at heavyweight respectively. The undercard, finally, will feature an awesome bantamweight matchup between Charles Jourdain and Marlon Vera, a heavyweight scrap between Tai Tuivasa and Robelis Despaign, and appearances from fighters like Edmen Shahbazyan, Casey O'Neill, and Giga Chikadze.

It will all kick off at 5:30 pm ET, with the main card beginning at 9:00.

As always, B/R will have you covered with complete results and highlights of all the action in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Drake Places Huge Bet on Joshua Van to Win UFC 331 Fight, 'I Don't Know Bro...But He Better Win'
articles.summary: Drake is heavily invested in UFC 331, particularly whether or not Joshua Van is able to retain the flyweight championship in the main event.
articles.body:
Drake is heavily invested in UFC 331, particularly whether or not Joshua Van is able to retain the flyweight championship in the main event.

The rap superstar posted a picture on his Instagram Story of his $650,000 bet on Van to defeat Alexandre Pantoja.

"I Don't Know Bro...But He Better Win," Drake wrote in the caption with the image.

The payout for Drake would be $1,098,000 if Van is able to win.

Drake is no stranger to placing large bets on sporting events. His biggest known wager to date is a $1.5 million bet on Argentina to beat Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.

That one didn't pan out with Spain defeating Argentina 1-0 in extra time.

Van, who is only 24, already has a 17-2 record in his professional MMA career. He has won seven consecutive bouts with three of the last four coming via stoppage.

Pantoja is getting a rematch with Van after their previous bout at UFC 323 ended in the first round due to an elbow dislocation when he was pushed to the ground. He had won eight straight matches prior to the accidental injury.

articles.title: John Hedges vs Pat Brown: Manchester-born Brown wins British and Commonwealth titles
articles.summary: Pat Brown continues his perfect start to life as a professional with a seventh successive stoppage to hand John Hedges his first defeat in front of a raucous Manchester crowd.
articles.body:
Pat Brown displayed destructive power to stop John Hedges in the sixth round and claim the British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles in Manchester.

Brown started slowly in front of a home crowd at Co-op Live Arena but was rewarded when he got behind his jab.

A thudding left hook to the body dropped Hedges in round six and he landed the same shot moments later to wrap up victory.

An emotional Brown, 26, spoke of how "special" it was to win the British title in his hometown.

"I don't care about all of the belts, it's for my family and my people," Brown said on DAZN.

"I've had a childhood with them all but I had to go off-grid to train and they've always stayed behind me.

"And for Ross - my cousin, who I love dearly - I said to him I would go all the way and I will."

Brown extends his perfect professional record to seven victories, with each of those coming via knockout, while Hedges lost for the first time in his 13-fight pro career.

Dreams of Old Trafford - Brown targets British title and famous nights

This fight was originally set to take place in Altrincham, but Matchroom made the switch to East Manchester's Co-op Live because of ticket demands.

And the 5,000-strong crowd made themselves heard when Brown entered the ring first, followed by a chorus of boos for Essex fighter Hedges.

Chants of 'Oh Patrick the Bomber' and 'Sale' rang around the arena as Hedges took the upper hand in the opening rounds with his awkward style.

Brown looked for ways to set up his heavy power-punches, but Hedges' sharp footwork and holding at the right time nullified the threat.

The pendulum started to swing in Brown's favour in the fifth when he began using his jab to set up combinations, with a right uppercut punctuating the round.

Hedges paid tribute to Manchester icon Ricky Hatton at the weigh-in after the first anniversary of his death passed on 14 September.

And it was a Hatton-like rippling left hook to the body from Brown that sent Hedges crashing to his knees.

Hedges beat the count but was sent tumbling back down to the canvas with another blow to the midsection - this time he was unable to pull himself back to his feet.

Family man Brown, who made his ringwalk with his father, had previously said "putting belts on his dad's shoulders" was all that mattered.

After Moses Itauma and Conor Benn both experienced losses when skipping the British title route and heading straight for world title glory, Brown said he wants to go on the "journey".

Chris Billam-Smith and Lawrence Okolie are two examples of those who have recently held the British cruiserweight title and gone on to win world honours.

Brown now holds the British and Commonwealth titles, and could look to European title-holder Viddal Riley next.

Riley, 29, last fought in April when he secured a unanimous points decision win over former world title challenger Mateusz Masternak.

When speaking to BBC Sport on Wednesday, the view of Old Trafford - the home of his beloved Manchester United - sat in the background.

Not since 1993, when Chris Eubank and Nigel Benn's unification bout ended in a draw, has the stadium hosted a boxing match.

Brown said one day headlining at Old Trafford would mean more to him than belts.

Most importantly, Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn sees the vision: "Pat Brown, world championship, Old Trafford. I see it."

Brown still has a long way to go if he's to be mentioned in the same breath as former world champion Hatton, but he's used his latest opportunity to make his mark.

articles.title: UFC 331 ‘Van vs. Pantoja 2’ play-by-play, results & round scoring
articles.summary: Sherdog's live UFC 331 “Van vs. Pantoja 2” coverage will begin Saturday at 5:30 p.m. ET.
articles.body:
Joshua Van (125) vs.Alexandre Pantoja (125) Arman Tsarukyan (156)vs. Mauricio Ruffy (155) Patricio Freire (145.5)vs. Doo Ho Choi (146) Alonzo Menifield(205.5) vs. Iwo Baraniewski (206) Gable Steveson (240) vs.Sean Sharaf (241) Marlon Vera (136) vs.Charles Jourdain (135) Tai Tuivasa (264.5)vs. Robelis Despaigne (263) Michael Aswell Jr.(146) vs. Joo Sang Yoo (145.5) Ryan Gandra (186) vs. OsmanDiaz (186) Edmen Shahbazyan(185) vs. Brunno Ferreira (184.5) Casey O'Neill (125) vs.Eduarda Moura (125.5) Giga Chikadze (146)vs. Joanderson Brito (145.5) Sherdog's live UFC331 "Van vs. Pantoja 2" coverage will begin Saturday at 5:30p.m. ET.

UFC 331 live results for Joshua Van vs. Alexandre Pantoja 2 andthe full fight card

GigaChikadze (146) vs. JoandersonBrito (145.5)

Featherweights light the fuse for UFC 331 at Crypto.com Arena inLos Angeles, where Chikadze (15-6, 8-4 UFC) awaits Brito (19-5-1,7-3 UFC) at 145 pounds. Frank Trigg administers the law and orderand gives the two combatants the green light. Front kick to thebody from Chikadze, who follows it with a straight left. Britoplows forward behind punches. Chikadze circles away from danger andcuts loose with a series of kicks, including several to the body.He throws a high kick and slips. Brito drives into top position and gets busy with ground-and-pound,increasing the intensity of his blows with each passing second. Heturns to repeated hammerfists and pounds away on a clearlydazed-and-confused Chikadze, resulting in the stoppage .

Joanderson Brito def. Giga Chikadze—KO (Punches) 1:57 R1

CaseyO'Neill (125) vs. EduardaMoura (125.5)

Attention at UFC 331 shifts to the women's flyweight division, asO'Neill (11-2, 6-2 UFC) puts Moura (12-2, 3-2 UFC) to the test at125 pounds. Jason Herzog polices the proceedings. No glove touch.Moura comes out firing and knocks O'Neill off-balance. She catchesa kick and trips O'Neill to the floor, settling in half guard.Moura drops elbows and a few short punches. Crowd boos the lack ofaction, as Herzog hovers nearby. O'Neill reclaims full guard, buther Brazilian opponent postures and punches. Moura moves from halfguard to north south and lures O'Neill into an anaconda choke. Sheloses her grip after a few tense moments and returns toground-and-pound. O'Neill elevates the Brazilian, rotates her hips and transitions toa belly-down armbar in one fluid motion. Moura taps in what canonly be described as a stunning and spectacular turn of events .Clear "Submission of the Year" contender.

Casey O'Neill def. Eduarda Moura—Submission (Armbar) 3:22 R1

Next on the UFC 331 docket: a middleweight clash between Shahbazyan(16-6, 9-6 UFC) and Ferreira (15-4, 6-4 UFC) at 185 pounds. MikeBeltran provides the oversight. They start with a cordial glovetouch. Shahbazyan takes the center of the cage and scores with alow kick. Ferreira circles on the outside. More leg kicks fromShahbazyan. Ferreira not yet in gear with 90 seconds gone. Heswitches to southpaw, and Shahbazyan starts to attack the otherleg. Double jab from Shahbazyan. Beltran warns Ferreira forextending his fingers. Midway through the round. Shahbazyan stayson the low kicks and connects them to a one-two. Ninety seconds onthe clock. Shahbazyan stays patient, continues to throw leg kicksand evades the return fire. Surprisingly little output fromFerreira. Ferreira intercepts him with a left hook, resets andjabs. They trade at the end of the round. Sherdog Scores Brian Knapp scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan Tudor Leonte scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan Mike Sloan scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan

Back at it for Round 2. Shahbazyan again claims the center.Ferreira stomps at the lead leg and fires a side kick to the body.Shahbazyan drives home another kick to the lower leg. Ferreiraexplodes into a right hand but fails to follow up. Shahbazyananswers with a low kick, then gets back to his jab. They tradejabs, and Ferreira whiffs on a wild overhand right. Two minutes togo in the round. Nice one-two from Shahbazyan, then doubles up onhis jab. Ferreira misses with a spinning elbow but resets andconnects with a right hand. Hard leg kick from the Brazilianfollowed by a right hand over the top. Shahbazyan lands two bodykicks, then another. Ferreira stomps at the lead leg. Shahbazyananswers with a one-two. They exchange punches, and Ferreira catchesan eye poke. Stern warning from Beltran as the round concludes. Sherdog Scores Brian Knapp scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan Tudor Leonte scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan Mike Sloan scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan

Ferreira might need a finish with five minutes to go. He ups theaggression right out of the gate and steps into a right hand.Shahbazyan kicks at the leg. Ferreira knees the body and fires offpunches in combination, then jabs. Shahbazyan circles back to thecenter and returns to his low kicks. Ferreira answers with one ofhis own. Sharp one-two from Shahbazyan, who dodges a spinning elbowand counters with a low kick. Midway through the round. Hard bodykick from Shahbazyan, who resets and fires a left hook to theliver. Ferreira responds with a right hand over the top. Shahbazyanavoids a flying knee and clinches along the fence. The crowd booshis efforts. Ninety seconds on the clock. Shahbazyan scores withknees to the legs and drives into a takedown. Ferreira standswithout issue but cannot break free. Shahbazyan lands an elbow asthey separate, jabs, changes levels and presses into the clinch.Ferreria lands a left hand on the break. Shahbazyan rocks theBrazilian with a jab and follows with a left hook, then floors himwith a right hand near the end of the round. Sherdog Scores Brian Knapp scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan (30-27Shahbazyan) Tudor Leonte scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan (30-27Shahbazyan) Mike Sloan scores the round: 10-9 Shahbazyan (30-27 Shahbazyan)

Edmen Shahbazyan def. Brunno Ferreira—Unanimous Decision (29-28,29-28, 30-27)

Action at UFC 331 stays in the middleweight division, where Gandra(10-1, 2-0 UFC) locks horns with Diaz (10-4, 1-2 UFC) at 185pounds. Jonathan Romero adjudicates matters. Off they go. Theycircle one another in the center. Romero issues an early warningfor extended fingers. Low kick from Gandra, who jabs to the bodyand throws a left hook upstairs. Diaz lands a jab, along with astanding elbow and an inside leg kick. Vicious multi-punch combination from Gandra backs up his opponent.He pins the shelled-up Diaz to the fence with punches, drops himwith an overhand right and finishes with more unabatedpunches .

Ryan Gandra def. Osman Diaz—TKO (Punches) 2:04 R1

MichaelAswell (146) vs. Joo SangYoo (145.5)

Featherweights step back into the UFC 331 spotlight, as Aswell(11-5, 1-3 UFC) squares off with Yoo (9-1, 1-1 UFC) at 145 pounds.Herb Dean answers the call as the third man in the cage and setsthem in motion. Yoo opens with a spinning back kick to the body.Aswell bobs, weaves and feints. Hard low kick from Yoo, who followsit with a jab. Aswell scores with a leg kick, then paws with hislead hand. Strong leg kick from Aswell. Yoo answers with his jabbut eats a right hand on the return. More low kicks and jabs fromYoo. Aswell follows a series of feints with a powerful overhandright. They exchange punches in the center of the cage, with bothmen landing with significant impact. Strong leg kick from Aswell,who cuts off a takedown with a front headlock, lands a knee and aleft hand on the break. Yoo gets back to his jab. Another wildexchange between the two featherweights. More jabs from Yoo. Aswellresponds with a right hand over the top and a low kick. He blocks awheel kick before they trade jabs. Another low kick from Aswell,who backs it up with a one-two. Yoo clinches along the fence as theround concludes. Sherdog Scores Brian Knapp scores the round: 10-9 Aswell Tudor Leonte scores the round: 10-9 Aswell Mike Sloan scores the round: 10-9 Aswell

Yoo circles on the outside and jabs, staying light on his feet.Aswell continues to feint, throwing the occasional overhand right.He ducks into a jab and lands a strong leg kick, followed byanother. Aswell shoots and settles in the clinch, firing knees tothe body. Fans boo, predictably. More knees to the body fromAswell, who holds double underhooks. He mixes in a few shoulderstrikes before they separate. Yoo answers a low kick with athree-piece combination. Aswell backs him up with an overhandright, then gives him pause with another leg kick. They trade jabs.Yoo sneaks in a left hook and backs it up with a jab. Yoo slipswhile throwing a kick, allowing Aswell to clinch briefly. Thirtyseconds to go in the round. Stout jab from Yoo. He ducks in on anattempted takedown but goes nowhere. Sherdog Scores Brian Knapp scores the round: 10-9 Yoo Tudor Leonte scores the round: 10-9 Yoo Mike Sloan scores the round: 10-9 Aswell

Still anyone's fight entering the final round. Double jab from Yoo.Aswell lands a leg kick, then another. Yoo answers with his jab.More leg kicks from Aswell, who sneaks in a right hand. Nice jabfrom Aswell, who lands a left hook and follows with a right handover the top. Yoo strikes in combination, as he ups his output andaggression. They clinch in the center of the cage. Yoo secures atakedown midway through the round. Aswell tries to get to his feet,then clings to the neck. Yoo moves to half guard and scores with afew shoulder strikes. Ninety seconds to go. Fans grow restless.Aswell squirms underneath his opponent. Yoo flirts with anarm-triangle and passes to side control. Aswell scrambles to hisfeet and clinches against the cage. They exchange in the waningseconds. Sherdog Scores Brian Knapp scores the round: 10-9 Yoo (29-28Yoo) Tudor Leonte scores the round: 10-9 Yoo (29-28 Yoo) Mike Sloan scores the round: 10-9 Yoo (29-28 Aswell)

Michael Aswell Jr. def. Joo Sang Yoo—Split Decision (28-29, 29-28,29-28)

articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live TONIGHT (Sat., Sept. 19, 2026) with UFC 331 taking place at crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, Ca., streaming exclusively live on Paramount+ . The main event is a rematch for the UFC Flyweight title with Joshua Van vs. Alexandre Pantoja 2.

Joshua Van gets a chance to defend his UFC Flyweight title for the second time tonight when he meets former champion Alexandre Pantoja . Van was, of course, awarded the belt after Pantoja went down with an arm injury early in their first fight last year. Since then Van solidified his title as champion by beating Tatsuro Taira in one of the fights of the year. This is Pantoja's first fight back since suffering that arm injury.

The co-main event tonight is a five round non-title fight in the Lightweight division. Arman Tsarukyan vs. Mauricio Ruffy could fast-track someone to a title shot with Justin Gaethje. For Tsarukyan that would be his second title shot, if you count the one he lost on weigh-in day (due to a back injury) before he was supposed to fight Islam Makhachev. Ruffy has never been this close to a title shot, but a win here on the back of his White House demolition job on Michael Chandler would be a big statement.

The main card is rounded out by Patricio Pitbull vs. Doohoo Choi , Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski and Gable Steveson vs. Sean Sharaf . This will be Pitbull's final fight on his current UFC deal. Iwo Baraniewski is worth keeping tabs on. He's won all his UFC fights so far in electrifying fashion. Steveson is, again, on course to be one of the biggest favorites in MMA betting history, that's in spite of him being just 4-0 as a pro.

The Featured 'Prelim' tonight is Marlon Vera vs. Charles Jourdain in the Bantamweight division. That portion of the card also has Robelis Despaigne vs. Tai Tuivasa , Michael Aswell vs. Joo Sang Yoo and Ryan Gandra vs. Ozzy Diaz .

The Early 'Prelims' kick us off with Giga Chikadze vs. Joanderson Brito . The early part of the show also includes Casey O'Neill vs. Eduarda Moura and Edmen Shahbazyan vs. Brunno Ferreira .

It's standard operating procedure tonight. Here's when the various portions of the latest numbered event goes live:

UFC 331 's Early "Prelims" will begin at 5:30 p.m. ET .

UFC 331 's Late "Prelims" are scheduled to start at 7 p.m. ET .

UFC 331 's PLE main card goes live at 9 p.m. ET .

All of UFC 331 airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here .

The live blog will get underway at 5:30 p.m. ET, just before the first fight. Come in and chat with your fellow Maniacs in the comments.

125 lbs.: Joshua Van vs. Alexandre Pantoja

155 lbs.: Arman Tsarukyan vs. Mauricio Ruffy

145 lbs.: Patricio Pitbull vs. Doo Ho Choi

205 lbs.: Alonzo Menifield vs. Iwo Baraniewski

265 lbs.: Gable Steveson vs. Sean Sharaf

135 lbs.: Marlon Vera vs. Charles Jourdain

265 lbs.: Tai Tuivasa vs. Robelis Despaigne

145 lbs.: Michael Aswell Jr. def. Joo Sang Yoo by split decision (28-29, 29-28, 29-28)

185 lbs.: Ryan Gandra def. Ozzy Diaz by TKO (punches), round 1 (2:04) — HIGHLIGHTS

185 lbs.: Edmen Shahbazyan def. Brunno Ferreira by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 30-27)

125 lbs.: Casey O'Neill def. Eduarda Moura by submission (armbar), round 1 (3:22) — HIGHLIGHTS

145 lbs.: Joanderson Brito def. Giga Chikadze by KO (hammerfists), round 1 (0:57) — HIGHLIGHTS

Michael Aswell Jr. vs. Joo Sang Yoo: The crowd weren't in love with this one. These two patiently traded strikes in a pretty low intensity kickboxing match for the first two rounds (which Aswell was clearly winning). In the third, Yoo felt some urgency and started to land some big shots and then got a takedown. Yoo needed a finish then, but didn't do nearly enough to make one happen.

Official decision: Michael Aswell Jr. def. Joo Sang Yoo by split decision (28-29, 29-28, 29-28)

Ryan Gandra vs. Ozzy Diaz: Gandra took a minute or so to size up Diaz. After that he blitzed forwards and rocked Diaz with a combo. Gandra didn't wait around and admire his work, he kept throwing and put Diaz down along the fence for yet another quick TKO.

Official decision: Ryan Gandra def. Ozzy Diaz by TKO (punches), round 1 (2:04)

Edmen Shahbazayan vs. Brunno Ferreira: Ferreira looked lean, but it took him until the third round to look mean. Shahbazyan kept him at bay early with calf kicks. Ferreira responded with teeps to the knee, which Shahbazyan seemed to think was illegal. In the third Ferreira tried to bring the chaos, but it was too little too late.

Official decision: Edmen Shahbazyan def. Brunno Ferreira by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 30-27)

Casey O'Neill vs. Eduarda Moura: Wow! O'Neill got taken down off the first kick she threw. Moura then smothered her and was close on an anaconda choke. O'Neill stayed calm, though. After the threat of the choke was over, O'Neill used the butterfly guard to push Moura into the air and then she caught Moura in an armbar on the way down. And then she made her tap!

Official decision: Casey O'Neill def. Eduarda Moura by submission (armbar), round 1 (3:22)

Giga Chikadze vs. Joanderson Brito: Chikadze started very well, stinging Brito with a blocked head kick. Chikadze was really flowing after that, but then he slipped on a kick attempt. Brito then got on top of him and unloaded! He put Chikadze out with brutal hammerfists.

Official decision: Joanderson Brito def. Giga Chikadze by KO (hammerfists), round 1 (0:57)
